stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO range of $70 to $78 a share and starts its roadshow
stories.standfirst: The company's own filing details 825 million Class A shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, correcting the draft terms reported on Monday.
body: Anthropic opened its roadshow on Tuesday. The offering is 825,000,000 Class A shares at $70 to $78 each: 801,351,354 from the company and 23,648,646 from existing holders, with a 30-day underwriter option on a further 123,750,000. The shares are to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as ANT, and the registration statement is not yet effective.

This replaces yesterday's account. Forbes reports that a draft sent to banks on Monday showed about 867 million shares at $70 to $80 and a raise of up to $69.3bn, and that Anthropic told underwriters those figures were wrong. At the top of the new range the raise is up to $64.4bn. A separate $26bn private placement with AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC takes the total to as much as $90.4bn, and about 20 per cent of the offer is reportedly set aside for retail investors.

Valuation figures differ. Forbes cites the Wall Street Journal and AP for about $1.3tn fully diluted, says Reuters calculated up to $1.02tn on shares outstanding, and notes some outlets used $1.4tn; the filing itself states no valuation. Reported financials are about $17bn of third-quarter revenue, a $567m operating loss and roughly $900bn of compute commitments.
Dario Amodei is due to appear in a livestream with Jamie Dimon on Friday. CNBC, as cited by Forbes, expects pricing on Wednesday 18 November and first trading on Thursday 19 November.

stories.headline: First day of Abu Dhabi talks ends without detail; prisoner swaps and territory discussed
stories.standfirst: Both sides report movement on exchanges, while the question of Donbas territory has been pushed to leaders.
body: The first day of the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks lasted about four and a half hours, with a 40-minute break, according to TASS as quoted by the Kyiv Post. They are the first face-to-face Russian and Ukrainian talks since February. Vladimir Medinsky led Russia, Rustem Umerov Ukraine, and Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner the US. Marco Rubio called the day very productive and Kushner said the US had narrowed the gaps without giving specifics. RFE/RL says progress is unclear and Russia has shown no sign of dropping hard-line demands.

Volodymyr Zelensky, speaking in Copenhagen, said an exchange of 1,000 or 1,500 prisoners each had been discussed, and that Russia raised territory, which he said must be decided at leaders' level. The two sides dispute the map: Foreign Minister Sybiha says Ukraine still holds 20 per cent of Donbas, not the 10 per cent Moscow claims, and the Kyiv Post could not verify either figure.

Kyiv has proposed Black Sea and energy ceasefires and is waiting for Moscow's answer. Moscow wants to block Ukraine's NATO membership, and the US has asked it to accept Article 5-style guarantees for Ukraine. European governments and NATO were consulted separately.
Day two is today and is due to cover de-escalation, energy, the Black Sea and a possible leaders' meeting. The Kyiv Post, citing Axios, says US envoys could then travel to Moscow and Kyiv.

stories.headline: Trump says Iran war is 'effectively over'; Tehran denies talks and says strikes continue
stories.standfirst: Washington and Tehran give opposing accounts of both the military position and any diplomacy.
body: On Monday Donald Trump said Iran is militarily effectively over and that the US is keeping the status quo. He called further strikes quite unlikely but said US forces remain locked and loaded. He spoke after meeting Qatar's prime minister with Vice-President Vance present, and cited what he called the largest naval blockade in history and Iron Gate, a CENTCOM operation to cut weapons and revenue flowing across Iran's land borders and the Caspian. Brent crude fell to $92.

Iran disputes the picture. Mohsen Rezaei accused the US of fake news about imaginary talks, and Foreign Minister Araghchi denied a reported Vance-Rezaei meeting in Qatar, which had been relayed through Turkey's Kalin. Iranian outlets say strikes continue, with Qeshm Island reportedly hit; the US has not acknowledged any. Tasnim reports that Iran will not negotiate until the US meets seven conditions.
Euronews is the only page opened for this story, so the competing claims above are unverified by independent reporting.

stories.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, priced at $2/$10 per million tokens until 30 November
stories.standfirst: The model tops several agentic and coding benchmarks by Google's account, and its price doubles at the end of the month.
body: Gemini 4 Carbon costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, the same as Gemini 4 Argon. From 30 November the price rises to $4 and $20. Google's post gives no parameter count or context length.

Google reports first place on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity WANDR and Zapier AutomationBench at more than twice as low a cost per task as the next-best external model, and second on Artificial Analysis MKA. It also says Carbon leads SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym and CWE-bench v1. On Google's internal Project Fortify it scores 100 per cent scanning recall and 95 per cent triage precision. A cyber-specialised variant is limited to the Fairwind Program.

On safety, Google gives a per-attempt breach rate of 0.8 per cent against 3.1 per cent for Argon, and 0 per cent on the Gray Swan indirect prompt-injection benchmark. All figures are the company's own and none has been independently checked in the sources read.

Carbon is available on the paid Gemini API tier, in Gemini Enterprise and Antigravity, and to Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode. A /swarm multi-agent feature is in preview in Antigravity.

stories.headline: November Patch Tuesday fixes over 1,000 CVEs, with one exploited Outlook NTLM leak
stories.standfirst: The only bug confirmed as exploited is a moderate-rated Outlook spoofing flaw that sends NTLMv2 data to an attacker's server.
body: Microsoft rates CVE-2026-124194 Moderate, CVSS 6.5, but it is the one flaw confirmed exploited. An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted message file; when the victim opens it, Outlook connects to an attacker-controlled network location without an external-content warning, exposing NTLMv2 authentication data that can be cracked offline or relayed. The Preview Pane does not trigger it. Affected products are Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024. Microsoft credits a researcher called nono and Benoit Sevens, and its acknowledgement notes that Sevens used Anthropic's Claude.

The critical fixes listed by Tenable include CVE-2026-118146, an authenticated Active Directory Domain Services RCE at CVSS 8.8; CVE-2026-118207, an Exchange RCE at 8.8; CVE-2026-119952, an unauthenticated Schannel RCE at 8.1; and CVE-2026-113862, a Windows NAT RCE at 8.1. A SharePoint elevation-of-privilege bug, CVE-2026-120002, scores 9.9 but is rated Important.

This is the last security update for Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education. Totals differ by tracker: Tenable counts 1,093 CVEs and SecurityWeek 1,094. The details come from a developer write-up of those vendors' figures, not from Microsoft's own pages.

sources.name: DEV Community write-up of Tenable and SecurityWeek data

stories.headline: McLaren show 2027 front-wing concept as Stella says Brazil win flattered the upgrades
stories.standfirst: Interlagos was McLaren's only upgrade package of the weekend; the team principal and Lando Norris disagree on how much it proved.
body: PlanetF1's technical feature on the Brazil package describes a front wing mounted to the second flap element rather than the mainplane, with a single active flap, the top one, that drops on the straights to cut drag. The mainplane is a continuous piece joined to the endplate's lower surface and is smaller because it no longer houses the nose pylons. McLaren's aerodynamics chief Peter Prodromou expects the concept to carry into the launch specification of next year's car, and the team accepts possibly slightly higher straight-line drag. No downforce or drag figures were given. PlanetF1 says McLaren alone brought upgrades to Brazil: front wing, rear wing, diffuser and floor.

Andrea Stella said the gain matched the predicted lap-time improvement, seen mainly in the dry, and that the weekend was more about the conditions and the car matching each other than the upgrades. He credited cool temperatures for tyre management, said long runs in heat still need work and flagged braking anomalies in Q2 that caused rear locking.

Norris, who won his third race of 2026, said McLaren is not yet at the level to fight for a world championship and is not confident in the package, with practice pace usually a tenth or two off the front. He said the upgrades worked and that without them the team would be further behind. Stella's formula1.com column calls the package a first step towards the 2027 car and says more parts arrive in Las Vegas.

stories.headline: Brazil strategy in numbers: Norris's lap-16 stop swung 6.4 seconds
stories.standfirst: A lap-by-lap analysis shows the undercut, not the pit-lane time, decided the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
body: Norris won by 14.602 seconds. He was 7.001s behind Kimi Antonelli at the end of lap 15, pitted on lap 16 for C5 softs with a 2.2s stop and gained 6.369s over the exchange, less than half a second of it from the pit lane. Antonelli stayed out one more lap on flat-spotted tyres with an unstable rear, and Norris passed him at Turn 1 on lap 20. Norris stopped again on lap 49 for fresh softs, and Oscar Piastri let him through. Both leaders switched to intermediates on lap 62, with Overtake Mode disabled by race control.

Max Verstappen started 21st after his engine penalty and was 13th after lap 1. He was 9.293s behind Norris after lap 38, when Isack Hadjar let him by. Red Bull pitted him on lap 45 for C5s, and he suspected damage; he cut the gap to 11.107s by lap 65. Hadjar stopped on lap 50 and finished third. George Russell ran 45 laps on his first set of slicks to finish fourth. Antonelli set the fastest lap, 1m12.689s, on lap 55 after his second stop on lap 53.

Stewards gave Antonelli five seconds for an unsafe release into Colapinto, and Oliver Bearman five seconds for one into Charles Leclerc; neither result changed. Leclerc was also given five seconds for contact with Liam Lawson and finished eighth.

stories.headline: DeepMind agents write 6.5 million lines of Lean proving Signal's protocol implementation
stories.standfirst: A paper claims machine-checked proofs of PQXDH and the Triple Ratchet down to machine-code level, in four weeks with five people.
body: Google DeepMind's paper, titled AlphaProof Code: Verifying Signal's Security at the Machine-Code Level, covers Signal's PQXDH key agreement and Triple Ratchet. A human-guided agent writes a Lean specification, and agents running Gemini Carbon then generated about 6.5 million lines of Lean to prove libsignal's implementation correct. The Lean kernel checks the proof.

The properties covered are forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security and handshake secrecy. The result is theoretical and assumes perfect cryptographic primitives, so it does not rule out side channels or implementation flaws outside the modelled code.
DeepMind says the work took four weeks with a team of five. The Register compares that with the roughly 20 person-years taken to verify the seL4 microkernel, though the two efforts differ in scope.

stories.headline: Burnham pledges £40m for GPs as consultants vote for a 48-hour strike
stories.standfirst: The Prime Minister said there is no money to settle the pay dispute but that he wants talks.
body: Speaking to LBC at Watford General Hospital, Andy Burnham announced £40m for GP practices this winter to identify and care for vulnerable patients. Consultants have voted for a 48-hour strike at the end of November over pay. Burnham said there is no money to settle the dispute and that he wants to talk first, and the Health Secretary has offered striking doctors talks.

The Strike Calendar, which warns it may be incomplete, lists BMA consultant action on 25 November. It also lists local NHS strikes at Lancashire Teaching Hospitals (Unite) and Leeds Teaching Hospitals (Unison).
Burnham also said the UK is stopping cyber attacks every day, including on the NHS, and called it a growing risk.

stories.headline: AMD details Zen 6: up to 256 cores in Venice and a claimed 27% IPC gain
stories.standfirst: The next Epyc generation comes in Zen 6 and Zen 6c variants with the same ISA and a reworked out-of-order core.
body: AMD told an event in Las Vegas last week that Zen 6 clocks run from 4.1 to 5.3GHz, with Venice Epyc reaching 256 cores. It claims an average 27 per cent IPC uplift on AI and server workloads, within a 20 to 31 per cent range over Zen 5 for cloud and AI.

The core gets a distributed out-of-order scheduler, a reworked front end and native FP16. VNNI-INT8 pipes go from two to four, and the core can do four AVX2 or two AVX-512 loads per cycle. L3 is 4MB per core: Venice uses eight CPU dies of 12 or 32 cores, giving 48MB or 128MB of L3 per die.
The Register's report gives no process node, TDP, pricing or launch date.

briefs.text: Google's Chrome 157 fixes CVE-2026-125350, an exploited use-after-free in the XML component and the eighth Chrome zero-day of 2026, in versions 157.0.8103.50/.51.
Barracuda says a small number of organisations have been hit by the chain of CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS 9.3) and CVE-2026-111560 (CVSS 8.6), which together give root on its email security gateways.
From 9 December Claude will be switched on by default in Microsoft 365 Copilot for UK tenants whose admins have made no choice, with data processed by Anthropic in the US.

The FIA's final engine-upgrade catch-up verdict finds Mercedes 2 to 4 per cent short of Red Bull Powertrains and grants it one extra upgrade each for 2026 and 2027, while Audi, Ferrari and Honda get two each.
The Republican-led US House voted 211-204 to refer Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively shelving it.
Gadi Eisenkot cancelled a preliminary coalition meeting with Likud due today after a speech by Netanyahu that he called delusional and divisive; no new date has been set.
